[pic=3]Right? This idea really echos with the idea of time as a whole.
[pic=1]Though we see time as a day to day thing, thousands of years ago, or thousands of years from now - so many things change, yet so much remains the same.

[pic=5]It’s interesting to consider though, if "time" is the "river," then we are the "water."

[pic=4]It’s not my greatest one. But I’ve captured a few concepts in this.
[pic=1]See Rascal, a difficult part of traditional haiku is the split of two ideas.
[pic=1]Two ideas that contrast each other, they vibrate against each other and change the context of each other.
[pic=4]The poem is meant to capture both, the phenomena of an instant of observing water, yet the realization that every droplet of water is new.
[pic=2]Each droplet that passes this place came from a glacier up above, and who knows, maybe it has made its way back here before.
[pic=1]Oh damn, that’s crazy. I’ve never considered the water flowing down this river is unique…
